## CY-A — New-root reading path
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7G-A] [MAP CY-A]
Trigger: DESIGNED — A successful, durable append_root() for an eligible new root starts the asynchronous job. A failed root write creates no job. [V10 §7G-A / THE ASYNCHRONOUS PERSISTENT LOCAL READING QUEUE]
Steps (in order):
1. C-7GA.3 — Queue activation and missing-job reconciliation — DESIGNED — Takes in: The one-time .nh_queue_activation.json boundary and durable roots after activation_root_count. Does: On startup, refuse reconciliation if the activation boundary is absent. Otherwise inspect roots beginning at activation_root_count + 1 and reconcile missing new-root jobs; never silently backfill earlier roots. Changes: Missing eligible jobs enter the same atomic enqueue operation used by live ingestion. [V10 §7G-A / QUEUE ACTIVATION BOUNDARY]
2. C-7GA.6 — Atomic enqueue and new-root identity — DESIGNED — Takes in: A durable root_id and enqueue_key = stable_hash(root_id + "reading_job_v1"). Does: Acquire the short .nh_enqueue.lock; look for that enqueue_key; append and flush one job only when absent; otherwise return the existing job_id regardless of its status; release the enqueue lock. Changes: One durable new-root job identity exists and ingestion releases without waiting for the mouth. [V10 §7G-A / ENQUEUE-LEVEL IDEMPOTENCY AND ATOMIC ENQUEUE]
3. C-7GA.7 — Full-job OS lock and claim — DESIGNED — Takes in: One pending job and the process-scoped .nh_queue.lock. Does: Acquire the non-blocking exclusive OS lock for the entire job; if unavailable, do no work. Write claim metadata, append job_claimed and in_progress, and check claim_id before every durable operation. Expiry metadata alone never permits takeover. Changes: One worker owns the processing interval until completion, clean failure or process death. [V10 §7G-A / JOB-PROCESSING LOCK AND CLAIM MECHANISM] [V10 §7G-A / WORKER PASS SEQUENCE — PRIMARY STEPS WITH CHECKPOINT SUBSTEPS]
4. C-7GA.10 — thread_membership_v1 — DESIGNED — Takes in: Derived source_title_type, thread_present, thread_root_count and the trigger's declared mode and reason. Does: Run thread_membership_v1. Manual bare/local-context overrides are allowed; live_ingestion may narrow only to bare with a nonempty reason. Reject other declared overrides. Without an accepted override, a confirmed real_thread or untitled_session with preceding context receives local-context; first-in-group, singleton, unresolved, missing or unrecognized classification receives bare. Never assign associative or combined: fall back to bare and record any implementation error. The raw title string never assigns the mode. Changes: The instruction records the assignment inputs, accepted or rejected override and actual reason. [V10 §7G-A / MODE-ASSIGNMENT RULE:]
5. C-7GA.8 — Reading-pass instruction and log — DESIGNED — Takes in: The assigned mode, target_root_id, job_id and a new pass_id. Does: Commit the immutable rpi_v1 instruction to .nh_reading_pass_log.jsonl before retrieval. [V10 §7G-A / THE READING-PASS INSTRUCTION AND LOG]

Changes: Only internally eligible material reaches retrieval; visible-output eligibility is not substituted for this internal gate. Otherwise compare same-root, same-thread and explicitly related readings; attach a repeat detection to the same clash rather than making a second object. Commit the clash result or no_clash_sentinel, then clash_detection_completed. Changes: A durable positive or negative clash result exists before view computation. 19. C-7GA.11 — Worker pass sequence — DESIGNED — Takes in: All triggered profile results and all three stage checkpoints. Does: Append computed_view_completed only when all profiles are accounted for, then append completed job status and release the OS lock. Terminal completed or failed jobs are never reselected. 20. C-7GA.13 — Queue-driven crash recovery — DESIGNED — Takes in: A restart, committed queue/pass/store evidence and the OS claim. Does: Exclude handled retryable technical failure from crash recovery. Stamp: NOT DECIDED    Source: [MAP CY-E]

A failed refresh preserves the prior snapshot with an honest later status event. Changes: The internal view may inform surfacing without becoming evidence or appearing unprompted. [V10 §7M] [04/NH_BUNDLE_4_LIVING_STATE_COMPUTED_VIEW_ACTION_AND_WORLD_MODEL_COMPLETION_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]

Does: Ask gently once; record derivation, reachability, assumptions, uncertainty and limits. Keep the six dispositions distinct: accepted and acted on, rejected, modified, postponed, ignored, alternative requested. [V10 §7N]
4. C-7N.7 — Action-family stage and level contract — ACCEPTED — Takes in: The actual current operation and the proposed later effect. Does: Keep current_action_state, current_authority_level, prospective_action_level, prospective_heightened_categories and advancement_requirements separate. Changes: The operation records actual partial or unknown work without false success or automatic repetition. Then evaluate top_security, recognized_ness, known_person with a valid PBR and any Ness-presence condition, otherwise guest. ## P-NEW-connection — Connection proposal → authorized acceptance → current use
Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [V10 §24] [04/NH_B_INT_8_CONNECTION_CAPABILITY_WAITING_AND_ACCEPTANCE_ROUTES_WIRING_v1_2_CANDIDATE.md §5]

Does: Keep source material, prior interpretation, assumption, unknown and invented simulation material separate. Record link type, decision status, independent certainty, authority, supporting evidence and correction history; acceptance never raises certainty. Changes: A direct-source accepted route or a properly grounded pending proposal has an honest basis. [V10 §24]
2. C-24.3 — Connection waiting area — DESIGNED — Takes in: A grounded connection proposal awaiting its permitted decision. Does: Keep undecided proposals indefinitely in the waiting area without force. Reject without repeatedly resurfacing unchanged evidence; genuine new evidence can produce a new linked proposal. Pending material may guide investigation only, not factual claims or lasting understanding. Changes: No pending proposal becomes accepted by age, repetition or retrieval. [V10 §24]
3. C-24.9 — Connection atomic compare-and-commit — ACCEPTED — Takes in: The canonical relationship key and exact durable authority event. Does: Use one recoverable compare-and-commit for duplicate comparison, accepted connection, authority proof/event identity, proposal decision when present and parent checkpoint. There is no accepted connection without recoverable direct-source, Ness-confirmation or narrow-rule proof. Changes: Concurrent attempts cannot create a second accepted record or a proofless acceptance. [04/NH_B_INT_8_CONNECTION_CAPABILITY_WAITING_AND_ACCEPTANCE_ROUTES_WIRING_v1_2_CANDIDATE.md §7]
4. C-24.14 — Connection current-use resolution — ACCEPTED — Takes in: The committed connection and later correction/dispute history. Does: Resolve the exact accepted ID/version, all later correction/dispute/supersession events, integrity and authority references, current relationship version, current-use state, separate original certainty, current privacy authorization and influence-removal status before each use. The proposed current-use states are current, disputed and corrected_or_superseded_for_current_use: carry a dispute and surface material uncertainty through the output gate; use a replacement only after its own checks. An unresolved, contradictory, unavailable or corrupt chain permits no use. Later events point back; the original accepted record and canonical key remain unchanged. Changes: Current consumers receive the actual usable relationship or a withheld/unresolved result. [04/NH_B_INT_8_CONNECTION_CAPABILITY_WAITING_AND_ACCEPTANCE_ROUTES_WIRING_v1_2_CANDIDATE.md §12C]

A candidate report is not a proposal and never automatically becomes one. Retrieval never accepts a relationship; co-retrieval never creates one. Exit: ACCEPTED — One current accepted connection with its recoverable authority trail, or a preserved undecided/rejected/failed outcome; original source records are neither changed nor merged. ## P-NEW-learning — Observation → grounded reading → outcome and adaptation
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §26] [V10 §22]
Trigger: DESIGNED — An authorized physical observation, actual reaction, action outcome or later relevant evidence reaches the continuous shared learning mechanism. [V10 §26.3] [V10 §26.6]
Steps (in order):
1. C-BOP — Behavioral Observation Processing (§25.1/§26) — DESIGNED — Takes in: Physical behavior and source-carried context under the actual observation permission. Does: Record only the physical event through the normal Catalog path; do not interpret emotion, motive or identity, and do not create a second behavioral memory. Changes: Preserved observations can become ordinary roots and readings. [V10 §25.1] [V10 §26.4]
2. C-7A — Universal Filter (§7A) — DESIGNED — Takes in: Eligible roots and permitted context supplied to the shared reader. Does: Apply the Universal Filter: preserve source and speaker, separate interpretation from evidence, keep possibilities rejectable and never decide a fact merely from an interpretation. Changes: The observation is eligible for a grounded revisable reading rather than a fixed label. [V10 §7A]
3. C-LEARN — Personal Learning and Adaptation (§26, cross-cutting) — DESIGNED — Takes in: Grounded readings, current shared state and the ongoing function's purpose. Does: Remain connected to the complete live mechanism before, during and after execution through LMAC. Calculate response behavior for the present moment; the thirteen personalization areas are views over shared material, not independent stores or fixed settings. Changes: The response uses current grounded context without maintaining a separate model of Ness. [V10 §26.2] [V10 §26.7] [V10 §26.8]
4. C-OOP — Outcome Observation Processing (§26) — DESIGNED — Takes in: Actual reaction evidence, outcome observations and uncertainty about absent reactions. Does: Route observations through the normal shared intake/reading path. Absence of objection is not approval and absence of reaction is not confirmation; a later observation may support a new reading without changing the earlier one. Changes: Outcome evidence remains separately sourced and eligible for later reconnection. [V10 §26.6]
5. C-AFFIRM — Off-board Affirmation Feedback Seam (§11 item 23) — DESIGNED — Takes in: An actual explicit response to a particular reading. Does: Keep the off-board response weightless and separate from the engine's operation; the engine never waits for affirmation and a response never becomes a truth score or authority. Changes: Presentation/current-use context may reflect the response while source readings remain unchanged. [V10 §11 item 23] [MAP C-AFFIRM]
6. C-22 — Wellbeing & Behavioral Baseline (§22) — DESIGNED — Takes in: Longitudinal authorized behavioral evidence and calibration anchors. Does: Compare sustained divergence against Ness's own baseline across multiple sessions. Keep the four tiers distinct: internal flag, informational mirror, REALITY-promotion throttling and REALITY-promotion freeze. Dry Mode and research remain available. Clinical/medical appointment material supplies the designed calibration anchor; exact empirical divergence thresholds remain unchosen. Changes: Only the designed wellbeing response changes; identity and speaker access do not follow from the tier. [V10 §22] [V10 §25.5]
7. C-LEARN.6 — Staged self-improvement authority and evidence — DESIGNED — Takes in: Grounded, varied and repeated outcome evidence meeting the actual authorized improvement boundary. Does: Make only the allowed staged adaptation; every automatic change is logged through OOP → Catalog → reading, explainable, root-traceable and reversible with prior state preserved. Safety, ownership, authority and architectural integrity never enter automatic self-rewriting. Changes: An allowed adjustment retains evidence and reversion history without changing the protected core. [V10 §26.9]
8. NOT DECIDED — Exact empirical thresholds, durations, calibration values and any complete adaptation execution/recovery mechanism left open by §26; no fixed preference profile or hidden certainty value is introduced.
Exit: DESIGNED — New observations/readings and honest outcome records coexist with earlier evidence; permitted response behavior is recalculated for the moment and protected-core authority remains unchanged. [V10 §26.7] [V10 §26.9]
Branches:
- DESIGNED — New roots enter CY-A; later materially relevant evidence enters CY-F. A possible action enters CY-E; an identity/security signal enters CY-I without using wellbeing as an access input. [V10 §26.9] [V10 §25.5] [V10 §7N]

## P-NEW-pairing — Owner-phone trust and recovery
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §25.7] [V10 §25.8] [V10 §25.9] [V10 §25.10]
Trigger: DESIGNED — Initial owner setup, an explicitly authorized replacement or local emergency recovery enters its own distinct trust sequence. [V10 §25.7] [V10 §25.9] [V10 §25.10]
Steps (in order):
1. C-PAIR.1 — Initial pairing lifecycle — DESIGNED — Takes in: The signed initial QR, temporary pairing secret and first phone's hardware-backed identity. Does: Keep qr_available scannable for 90 seconds. Successful first pairing makes the QR and secret permanently inert and sealed immediately, binds the hardware-backed identity and enters phone_provisionally_paired_qr_destroyed. Recovery setup may retry on that same phone without reopening the QR; final trusted-owner status waits for the complete first recovery-code handover. Changes: Initial QR pairing cannot be reused, and provisional trust is not permanent owner trust. [V10 §25.7]
2. C-PAIR.2 — Normal recovery-code lifecycle — DESIGNED — Takes in: The phone-encrypted new recovery code after biometric approval. Does: Display only on the phone until confirmation or 10 minutes 30 seconds. After Saved in Bitwarden, request four unique random character positions in exact order, case-sensitive, with three total attempts and fresh positions after failure; keep no positions, characters or comparison results. On success run the local non-effectful acceptance test, activate the new code, then invalidate the old code and seal the local copy. All three failures leave the new code inert and old code valid. Changes: The saved, verified, tested and activated code completes the handover; Bitwarden is the intended long-term copy. [V10 §25.8]
3. C-PAIR.3 — Future-phone replacement — DESIGNED — Takes in: The current normal recovery code and motherbase thumbprint through maintenance. Does: Require both for a future replacement phone. Revoke the previously trusted phone only after the new phone is fully paired and verified; rotate the normal code through the same complete handover. A revoked phone must repeat the full recovery flow to regain trust. Changes: Replacement preserves a single valid current owner-phone trust outcome. [V10 §25.9]
4. C-PAIR.4 — Atomic emergency recovery — DESIGNED — Takes in: Physical motherbase access, separate emergency code, printed sheet and motherbase thumbprint. Does: Keep the new phone provisional and all old trust/materials valid until new normal code, new emergency code and new printed sheet have each completed their required verification. One atomic final commit activates all new material, makes the new phone sole trusted phone, invalidates all old material and records bai_emergency_reset_finalized. Any pre-commit failure seals/inerts all provisional material, cancels provisional pairing, preserves all old validity and records bai_emergency_reset_aborted with step/reason. Remote emergency recovery is prohibited. Changes: Emergency recovery never partially revokes existing trust. [V10 §25.10]
5. C-2 — Ness Interaction and Artifact-Delivery Contract (§2, §2A — LOCKED) — DESIGNED — Takes in: The pairing or recovery interaction presented to the owner. Does: Keep the exact requested operation and required interaction boundaries; successful completion may not be claimed before the governing sequence actually completes. Changes: The interaction preserves the actual provisional, completed or failed state. [V10 §2] [V10 §2A] [MAP C-PAIR]
Exit: DESIGNED — Final owner trust exists only after the complete required handover or atomic emergency commit; a failed intermediate operation leaves its specified prior valid state intact. [V10 §25.7] [V10 §25.10]
Branches:
- DESIGNED — Device-trust change and emergency factors invoke P-NEW-maintenance with their exact purpose scope. Final trusted-owner facts may satisfy prerequisites in P-NEW-enrollment; they do not prove a voice is Ness. [V10 §25.13] [V10 §25.11]

Snapshot owner references and versions without taking over their authority. Changes: Only a complete fresh prerequisite set can precede the biometric request. Immediately before token consumption reread all six owners; if one changed, revoke through BAI and open nothing. Otherwise consume once, flush and bind BAI's proof, then commit enrollment_session_opened. Microphone capture requires that current commit. Changes: A biometric success alone neither opens capture nor identifies the voice as Ness. [04/NH_B_INT_7_INITIAL_NESS_VOICE_PROFILE_ENROLLMENT_BOOTSTRAP_WIRING_v1_1_CANDIDATE.md §5]

Does: Freeze the captured set, submit each observation through Catalog and B11 with capture_id end-to-end, record verified root outcomes and enqueue normal quarantine reading. A segment excluded from profile training is still preserved through the ordinary observation path, subject to privacy exclusion. Changes: No second staging, root, profile or reading store is created. [04/NH_B_INT_7_INITIAL_NESS_VOICE_PROFILE_ENROLLMENT_BOOTSTRAP_WIRING_v1_1_CANDIDATE.md §10]
5. C-ENROLL.9 — Initial-corpus eligibility gate — ACCEPTED — Takes in: One immutable segment and its authorization, quality and stream evidence. Commit one accepted or rejected segment outcome by identity; these checks prove a consistent live speaker, not who that speaker is. Changes: Only eligible segments may contribute accepted readings to the provisional profile. [04/NH_B_INT_7_INITIAL_NESS_VOICE_PROFILE_ENROLLMENT_BOOTSTRAP_WIRING_v1_1_CANDIDATE.md §11]

If readiness cannot be established, create no profile and propose no link. If established, freeze the enrollment_profile_input_bundle [proposed] containing exact readings, eligibility decisions, operation/session, prerequisite/authorization and readiness references; it is coordination only, not a profile or new identity evidence. Changes: A verified immutable input bundle exists without guessed sample counts or thresholds. [04/NH_B_INT_7_INITIAL_NESS_VOICE_PROFILE_ENROLLMENT_BOOTSTRAP_WIRING_v1_1_CANDIDATE.md §12] [04/NH_B_INT_7_INITIAL_NESS_VOICE_PROFILE_ENROLLMENT_BOOTSTRAP_WIRING_v1_1_CANDIDATE.md §12A]

Does: Propose enrollment_material_provisional with enrollment_provisional certainty and exact authority basis. Wait for current committed §7L-owned link truth; a proposal, acknowledgment, pending or stale result is insufficient. Only after the link may SIA create its idempotent provisional profile from eligible linked readings, never raw audio or logs. ## P-NEW-maintenance — Purpose-bound maintenance → change or rollback
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §25.13]
Trigger: DESIGNED — A declared exact code, configuration, security-policy, device-trust or emergency-recovery change requests its purpose-specific maintenance window. [V10 §25.13 / Entering Maintenance Mode]
Steps (in order):
1. C-BGMM.8 — Maintenance entry sequence — DESIGNED — Takes in: The recorded purpose and exact plain-language change before authorization. Does: Require the motherbase thumbprint. Code/configuration/security-policy changes also require trusted-phone confirmation using bgmm_confirmation:<session_id>:<purpose>; device-trust change instead requires the normal recovery code; emergency recovery requires physical motherbase access, separate emergency code and printed sheet. Open only the exact purpose/file scope after the required factors. Changes: A narrow maintenance window may grant a scoped write token, never general authority. [V10 §25.13 / Entering Maintenance Mode] [V10 §25.13 / Purpose-Specific Authorization]
2. C-BGMM.9 — Exact file-scope enforcement — DESIGNED — Takes in: The declared file list and each proposed write. Does: Permit only exact in-scope files. Emergency recovery is limited to device-trust records regardless of declaration; an out-of-scope write is blocked and immediately records bgmm_out_of_scope_write_attempt. Changes: Protected code/configuration cannot be reached through a recovery-purpose window. [V10 §25.13 / File Scope Enforcement] [V10 §25.13 / Purpose-Specific Authorization]
3. C-BGMM.10 — Protected change sequence — DESIGNED — Takes in: An authorized exact change with durable rollback capacity. Does: Before touching a file, flush its change-log entry and persist the encrypted full-content rollback package. Apply the change, record hash_after, update and re-sign the manifest, re-sign modified executables, then immediately write bgmm_change_applied. Any later step failure triggers rollback. Changes: The changed files have verifiable signatures and recovery evidence, or revert through the protected rollback path. [V10 §25.13 / Change Application]
4. C-BGMM.11 — Immediate automatic relocking — DESIGNED — Takes in: Completion, timeout, crash/restart, relevant security alert, phone loss, explicit abort or biometric expiry. Does: Close the window immediately, revoke the write token and record bgmm_write_token_revoked; rollback any partly applied change. Changes: No abandoned or failed window leaves write authority open. [V10 §25.13 / Automatic Relocking]
5. C-BGMM.12 — Idempotent rollback — DESIGNED — Takes in: The encrypted package's prior contents, hashes, signatures, metadata and signed-manifest history. Does: Decrypt and verify prior_hash against actual prior_content, restore exact content/signature/metadata and prior signed manifest. If a file already matches, do not write it again. On interrupted rollback, retry idempotently from actual file state; never use hashes as substitutes for backups. Changes: Exact prior protected state is restored or startup remains blocked by failure. [V10 §25.13 / Rollback] [V10 §25.13 / Crash, Restart, Offline Behavior]
6. C-BGMM.7 — Protected startup recovery worker — DESIGNED — Takes in: Startup integrity results and any incomplete rollback package. Does: Finish protected recovery and record rollback completion before N.H starts. Integrity failure prevents startup; repair is available only through the authorized maintenance route. No network is required. Changes: Startup proceeds only from verified protected state. [V10 §25.13 / Protected Startup Recovery Worker] [V10 §25.13 / Crash, Restart, Offline Behavior]
7. C-BGMM.14 — Maintenance privacy — DESIGNED — Takes in: Descriptions, phone confirmations, rollback metadata and security audit records. Does: Keep private content and secrets out of all these surfaces; log structural operations, file paths and hashes rather than protected contents. An open maintenance window never grants disclosure permission. Changes: Maintenance evidence remains useful without exposing protected memory. [V10 §25.13 / Privacy During Maintenance]
8. C-2 — Ness Interaction and Artifact-Delivery Contract (§2, §2A — LOCKED) — DESIGNED — Takes in: The maintenance declaration, exact change description and visible result. Does: Preserve the locked interaction/artifact contract throughout the proposed change and its outcome; a description does not authorize a broader action. Changes: The user-facing operation stays bound to its exact scope. [V10 §2] [V10 §2A] [MAP C-BGMM]
Exit: DESIGNED — The approved change is verified and relocked, or exact rollback completes before startup; unverifiable integrity keeps startup stopped. [V10 §25.13]
Branches:
- DESIGNED — Device-trust or emergency recovery returns to P-NEW-pairing under its distinct atomic finalization conditions. A new protected change requires its own P-NEW-maintenance authorization. [V10 §25.9] [V10 §25.10] [V10 §25.13]

Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_AUTHORITY_INTEGRITY_CONTROL_PLANE_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_10_CANDIDATE.md §9] [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §D]

Does: Before enumeration or content reads, resolve the shared caller-blind input-establishment episode from committed state and acquire its one claim. Equivalent callers attach separately to that same work. An exhausted episode receives no invented fresh anchor to evade B9; reuse of a prior outcome requires completed current-input re-proof. 2. C-NEW-AIC.3 — AIC-0 [proposed] through AIC-5 [proposed] — ACCEPTED — Takes in: The tentative governing membership, content identities, status evidence, authority order and derivation rules. Does: Enumerate once, recompute identities and fully revalidate the complete basis from actual sources. Seal by one compare-and-commit only if the complete observations match; only then derive a generation. Determinate absence or identity mismatch is evidence within that sealed basis; inability to read/recompute or changed establishment inputs is technical/incomplete work and commits no authority outcome. Changes: A generation exists only from its fully revalidated sealed basis. [04/NH_AUTHORITY_INTEGRITY_CONTROL_PLANE_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_10_CANDIDATE.md §9]
3. C-NEW-AIC.3 — AIC-0 [proposed] through AIC-5 [proposed] — ACCEPTED — Takes in: The sealed immutable basis for that generation. Does: Derive status and contradictions only from that basis; never refresh or substitute members inside the generation. Commit at most one snapshot or deterministic refusal per generation, then append the single run terminal before releasing any reference. A technical stop supplies no usable snapshot; no authority conflict is repaired or ranked away. Changes: The caller receives released proof or an exact stop, not permission or success evidence. 4. C-NEW-UDOK — Unified Durable Operation Kernel — ACCEPTED — Takes in: The committed operation identity, current generation, declared contract and typed owner references. At Layer 2, leave claims, reservations, per-effect authorization and per-use privacy/access/relevance with their exact owners and check references immediately before the protected effect. Never require nonexistent future owner records early or invent them. Changes: Coordination advances only as far as the next actual owner fence permits. Registration grants only membership: component admission, claim, authorization, retry and privacy/access/relevance still apply afterward at their owners. Before a successor generation, commit and revalidate the predecessor's UDOK-6C membership closure against its exact unchanged head; unresolved predecessor obligations still require owner recovery or explicit owner safe-supersession evidence. Changes: The complete permitted child population remains visible to current-generation terminal accounting without granting effect authority. [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §M] [04/NH_UNIFIED_DURABLE_OPERATION_KERNEL_MECHANICAL_DESIGN_v1_9_CANDIDATE.md §H]

- NOT DECIDED

## P-NEW-fabric — Candidate multi-index retrieval and rebuild
Stamp: CANDIDATE    Source: [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §15]
Trigger: CANDIDATE — A permitted retrieval purpose or an index loss/staleness condition invokes the candidate multi-index direction. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §17] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §19]
Steps (in order):
1. C-NEW-FABRIC — Provenance-First Multi-Index Memory Fabric — CANDIDATE — Takes in: Permitted preserved source records and declared accepted relationships. Does: Keep positional, semantic, temporal, entity/Person-Box, accepted-connection, story/theme/clash and operational-provenance channels distinct. Future state/world views require their own settled rules. Every real source item remains its own Origin; mixed media connect rather than merge and original/import/record times remain separate. Changes: Derived channel references never replace source memory or establish identity from similarity. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §16] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §18]
2. C-NEW-FABRIC.2 — Retrieval-plan record requirements — CANDIDATE — Takes in: The actual query purpose, permissions, channels, versions, health, parameters and selected context. Does: Preserve the retrieval-plan record with retrieved identities, exclusions/omissions, degraded status, relationship basis, evidence sent to the model and final context actually used. Keep the record as operational provenance, never another vote. Changes: The operation discloses what each channel actually contributed. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §17]
3. C-NEW-FABRIC.3 — Index rebuild and degradation — CANDIDATE — Takes in: Index loss, corruption, staleness or partial availability. Does: Rebuild only from permitted sources and accepted relationships; record visible degradation, use only bounded fallback, claim no complete retrieval and invent no missing link. Never delete or rewrite source memory or silently mix held, rejected, provisional, simulated or unauthorized material. Changes: Incomplete retrieval remains honestly incomplete. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §19] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §20]
4. NOT DECIDED — Concrete channel count, technologies, schemas, layout, ranking values, final retrieval-plan representation and complete execution/recovery mechanics.
Exit: CANDIDATE — Permitted labeled references and an honest retrieval provenance/degradation record, without a new memory authority. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §17] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §19]
Branches:
- NOT DECIDED

## P-NEW-lab — Candidate bounded laboratory correction loop
Stamp: CANDIDATE    Source: [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §22]
Trigger: CANDIDATE — An approved immutable laboratory run contract names the exact task, source snapshot, disposable workspace and authorized bounds. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §23]
Steps (in order):
1. C-NEW-LAB.1 — Immutable run contract requirements — CANDIDATE — Takes in: Exact task/success condition, source identity, workspace, read/write/forbidden scopes, commands, network, protected tests, budgets, stop/escalation and verification obligations. Does: Freeze the run contract before any correction loop; it alone supplies patch authority. B9 technical retry never authorizes a code redesign or wider patch. Changes: Every permitted laboratory action has declared scope and limits. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §23] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §25]
2. C-NEW-LAB — Bounded Self-Healing Execution Laboratory — CANDIDATE — Takes in: The disposable source copy and actual observed execution/test failure. Does: Run, observe failure, diagnose, make a bounded patch, test and repeat only within the immutable contract. Never modify authority/accepted/history files, protected tests, budgets or permissions; never access undeclared secrets, live private stores, network or production. Changes: A candidate correction advances only inside its authorized laboratory bounds. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §22] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §26]
3. C-NEW-LAB.2 — Append-only laboratory trajectory — CANDIDATE — Takes in: Every observation, command, file change, test, failure, correction, budget use and checkpoint. Does: Preserve the complete append-only trajectory and terminal evidence; hide no failed cycle and rewrite no history. Changes: The candidate has an inspectable full execution trail. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §23] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §26]
4. C-NEW-LAB.3 — Laboratory completion requirements — CANDIDATE — Takes in: All declared behavioral, regression, safety, identity, scope and trajectory checks. Does: Require every declared condition and an independent deterministic verifier; one chosen passing test or the agent's claim never establishes completion. Return only the candidate patch/artifact and evidence, without acceptance, merge, deployment or installation. Changes: The loop ends with bounded candidate evidence or a stopped incomplete result. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §24]
5. NOT DECIDED — Final laboratory technology, contract serialization, numeric budgets, verifier implementation and concrete kernel integration.
Exit: CANDIDATE — A candidate patch/artifact with its complete trajectory and independent verification result, or an honest stop; no production authority is created. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §24]
Branches:
- CANDIDATE — Future coordination can use P-NEW-durable, retaining contract-owned patch authority; a technical retry alone is not another authorized correction cycle. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §25]
- NOT DECIDED

## P-NEW-tools — Candidate capability selection and sandboxed tool forge
Stamp: CANDIDATE    Source: [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §28]
Trigger: CANDIDATE — A bounded capability request or candidate adapter proposal is evaluated against the present operation's authority and declared tool contract. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §29] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §30]
Steps (in order):
1. C-NEW-TOOLS — Governed Capability Registry and Sandboxed Tool Forge — CANDIDATE — Takes in: The operation's identity, purpose, mode, authority snapshot, privacy state and authorization. Does: Expose only capabilities allowed in that current context, never every installed tool. A successful call never proves its result true or safe, and an installed capability never authorizes every operation. Changes: The model receives only the bounded permitted inventory. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §29] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §32]
2. C-NEW-TOOLS.1 — Versioned capability contract requirements — CANDIDATE — Takes in: A versioned capability identity/executable hash, owner, schemas, purpose, location, data classes, read/write effects, prerequisites, risk, approval and resource/recovery contract. Does: Bind exact scopes, ceilings, idempotency, reversibility, logs, installation/suspension/revocation/replacement and dependencies. Never pass a credential or token beyond its audience/purpose, permit undeclared access or create a parallel privacy/authority gate. Changes: The capability's effect boundary remains explicit and inspectable. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §29] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §32]
3. C-NEW-TOOLS.2 — Non-callable tool-forge candidate lifecycle — CANDIDATE — Takes in: A model-generated or AI-assisted adapter candidate. Does: Keep it non-callable through bounded proposal, isolated source, static/dependency checks, schema/contract validation, unit/integration tests, adversarial/permission tests, protected-file/secret verification, independent audit and explicit acceptance for its stated scope. Signed registration/installation is a later separately authorized step; the model cannot activate its own output. Changes: Candidate code never becomes an active tool automatically. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §30]
4. NOT DECIDED — Exact signing, packaging, registration, installation, contract representation and complete runtime execution/recovery mechanisms.
Exit: CANDIDATE — A permitted existing capability selection or a non-callable candidate with bounded evidence; no acceptance or installation is implied by generation. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §28] [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §30]
Branches:
- CANDIDATE — Any actual external effect remains under CY-E authority, and outside research remains isolated under CY-C; the candidate registry creates neither a bypass nor a new automatic connection. [05/NH_DECISION_PACKAGE_FIVE_FRAMEWORK_CAPABILITY_ADDITIONS_v1.md §31]
- NOT DECIDED

## P-NEW-world — Confirmed World entry → presentation or approved simulation
Stamp: NOT DECIDED    Source: [V10 §19A]
Trigger: DESIGNED — A request to enter Ness's World begins identity confirmation; an ordinary command alone cannot open it. [V10 §19A]
Steps (in order):
1. C-19.2 — Three-step World opening — DESIGNED — Takes in: A World-opening request. Does: Confirm identity through private code or thumb/fingerprint, ask whether to open Ness's World, then require the separate confirmation. Do not merge the request, identity proof and opening choice. Changes: The World opens only after all three designed steps. [V10 §19A]
2. C-19 — Interface / Ness's World (§19) — DESIGNED — Takes in: The permitted memories, people, projects and presentation state. Does: Keep conversation available inside the World and preserve the blank-start governing rule, white wooden doors and deep navigation. Presentation may change automatically where useful but cannot secretly start an action or simulation. Changes: Presentation and navigation expose permitted material without becoming a new source of truth. [V10 §19A]
3. C-19.4 — World-manipulation boundary — DESIGNED — Takes in: A grab, move, merge, split, reshape, rewind or speed change to a World element. Does: Treat it as presentation/navigation or an explicitly labeled simulation by default. Never rewrite roots, readings, tellings, identity links, themes, state, permissions or deletion state, and never change an external system through a visual gesture alone. Changes: Any underlying-record or real-world effect requires a separate proposed authorized operation. [V10 §19A]
4. C-19.11 — Explicit simulation boundary — DESIGNED — Takes in: An explicit approved transition into simulation or requested generated voice. Does: Keep actual replay distinct from new simulation. A major simulation change requires approval; before a simulated voice, introduce Simulating voice in the normal voice with a gradual shift. Never begin a simulation secretly. Changes: Simulated content remains visibly simulated and separate from recorded reality. [V10 §19A]
5. C-19.21 — Wonder interface and selected-transfer boundary — ACCEPTED — Takes in: Wonder-origin material selected for possible memory transfer. Does: Apply the selected-only A17 boundary: selection/submission remains deliberate, surrounding scratch remains isolated, and origin/possibility status survives any later accepted use. Changes: The World interface creates no direct memory-entry route. [04/NH_A17_WONDER_TO_MEMORY_POLICY_PACKAGE_v1_0_CANDIDATE.md §2] [04/NH_A17_WONDER_TO_MEMORY_POLICY_PACKAGE_v1_0_CANDIDATE.md §4] [04/NH_A17_WONDER_TO_MEMORY_POLICY_PACKAGE_v1_0_CANDIDATE.md §5]
6. NOT DECIDED — Complete World/simulation session operation identity, transaction/recovery mechanics and undecided interface choices. Accepted UE5 direction does not promote every candidate blueprint detail to accepted behavior.
Exit: NOT DECIDED
Branches:
- DESIGNED — A real underlying-record or outside effect enters CY-E or its specialist path; visible conversation follows CY-B. [V10 §19A]
- ACCEPTED — Deliberate selected Wonder transfer is governed by CY-J's A17 branch, whose mechanical route remains open. [04/NH_A17_WONDER_TO_MEMORY_POLICY_PACKAGE_v1_0_CANDIDATE.md §4] [04/NH_A17_WONDER_TO_MEMORY_POLICY_PACKAGE_v1_0_CANDIDATE.md §9]

## Cross-piece USED BY continuations — path uses

Each owner table adds one row for each decided path step. The using place is one canonical part, followed by one path and step; it is never a bare path or a group of part IDs. A row describes the source-defined use within that path, including use of a governing rule. It adds no extra execution, scheduler, permission or automatic branch. Both ends are named by the owner heading and the using cell; the matching TOGETHER continuation follows. Every Source cell is populated independently of the other cells.

Every canonical card has a placement below. Direct entries name its step; inherited entries place the card under its canonical owning component or sub-part. Inherited placement means that the existing source-defined detail is carried by that owner's path, subject to its own stamp, gates and branch; it does not say that every descendant executes on every traversal. ## Named review dispositions

Each positive scan hit has its own location and disposition. Ordinary totals are recounted separately. The ten empty-failure hits below were checked against all six ALONE boxes, the parent constraint and the USED BY rows; the source gives no independent failure class for those atoms. The parent no-run and durable-accounting requirements remain explicit.

| Card / line | Flag | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| C-7GA.15.2.3.1 — Configuration who; line 672 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The source names who as version provenance but gives no separate actor-field failure outcome. Invalid configuration still blocks the run under C-7GA.15.2 and C-7GA.15.12. |
| C-7GA.15.2.3.2 — Configuration when; line 695 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The source names when as version provenance but chooses no separate timestamp-field failure outcome; invalid configuration still blocks activation. |
| C-7GA.15.2.3.3 — Configuration basis; line 718 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The source names basis as version provenance but chooses no independent basis-field failure class; the configuration and run prerequisites remain intact. |
| C-7GA.15.3.2 — Trigger source; line 841 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The source requires trigger source at receipt without a separate field-level failure transition. Durable receipt and no-lost-request behavior remain on the parent. |
| C-7GA.15.3.3 — Trigger receipt time; line 864 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The receipt-time atom has no independently decided failure outcome. The parent still requires durable identity/source/time at receipt. |
| C-7GA.15.7.2 — Run trigger provenance; line 1282 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The composite provenance element has no independent failure class. Source and identity are separately decomposed and the run retains its parent-context connection. |
| C-7GA.15.7.2.1 — Run trigger source; line 1308 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The run trigger-source field has no separate failure outcome; the prohibition on invented provenance remains explicit. |
| C-7GA.15.7.2.2 — Run trigger identity; line 1331 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The run trigger-identity field has no separate failure outcome. Parent and child identities remain distinct and connected. |
| C-7GA.15.10.1 — No activation store scan; line 1674 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | The atom is an unconditional prohibition on activation store scanning, not a newly designed scanner with an invented failure/recovery mechanism. |
| C-7GA.15.13.3 — Retry and recovery event references; line 2012 | prerequisite_review / Fails closed by | Retry/recovery events are append-only references under their actual operation; B12 supplies no independent event-writer failure class. |
